do_more: Use clear, single-phrase hooks that hint at a twist (e.g., 'Trap', 'Curve', or quirky noun)
Keep titles concise (<4 words) and avoid vague descriptors like 'detour' or 'panic' unless paired with a unique angle
Focus on relatable, everyday psychology concepts that can be visualized in 42 s
Use humor and doodle animation to illustrate the concept in a punchy, memorable way
Highlight an emotional payoff (confidence, relief, curiosity) early in the first 5 s
avoid: Avoid generic or overly broad titles that lack a hook word
Don’t use the 'detour' or 'panic' style that has been rejected
Keep videos longer than 45 s; stick to the standard 42‑s length
Skip over‑explanation or slow pacing—maintain a brisk narrative
short.title_style: Short, hook‑first titles that pair a single, intriguing word with a clear concept—e.g., ‘The Confidence Curve’ or ‘The Sunday Panic Trap’—capture curiosity and promise a twist in a single glance.
next_tests: Experiment with a 30‑s tight version of a hit concept to test retention vs. 42‑s standard
Create a new series titled ‘The X Effect’ (e.g., ‘The Mirror Effect’) to gauge if a fresh hook drives shares
Run A/B on adding a playful emoji to the title (e.g., ‘The Confidence Curve 🚀’) to see if visual cues boost clicks
